challenge.better_approach: Clearing at the PROVED crossing itself was looked at: it would need a hook in transitions for every terminal crossing (SUPERSEDED, RETIRED, ...), and it would not reach troubles already standing over tickets that went terminal earlier, like 8c5fdb750b75. A cleanup recheck covers both, in the same shape as the findings and seals steps.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a terminal ticket never asks a gate again. Measured: the workflow grammar's TERMINAL_STATES end the path, and queueme runs only on a crossing. If a terminal ticket were reopened, its next refusal would raise afresh.
challenge.prior_art: 41a5bae3d01b (clear on take) and 794835a34ec9 (clear on pass) in cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py; 17b087f2483f's recheck in cairn/devices/tester/recheck.py and its cleanup step.
challenge.real_collision: none: the clear rides the ticket's own DiagnosticBase door and the trouble device still folds it (Law 6).

answers.falsifier: Done when a PROVED ticket's raised trouble clears through bin/cairn cleanup while a FIXME ticket's stands; wrong intent if a terminal ticket can still be asked again at the gate that raised it.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the sibling ticket ticket 17b087f2483f's bounds named for ticket-unqueued-*/ticket-refused-* at cairn/machines/ticket, measured live as ticket-unqueued-8c5fdb750b75-at-clearance standing over a PROVED ticket (cairn trouble live)
answers.how: A recheck() in cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py plus a --recheck CLI; a tickets step in bin/cmd/cleanup hands it the live ids; the ticket emits clear_trouble for each terminal ticket whose raise stands on its trail; the drain folds. Red-first proof cairn/machines/ticket/proofs/test_a_terminal_ticket_clears_its_ticket_troubles.py.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth stays true; a trouble standing over a PROVED ticket tells the inbox reader something false.
answers.what: cairn cleanup clears a ticket's own ticket-unqueued-* and ticket-refused-* troubles once the ticket stands at a terminal state, since a terminal ticket never asks the gate again.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-19: a --recheck CLI under python -m built its Ticket from __main__ and read every raise as absent (the trail is named after the module); the CLI must call the named module.

title: cairn cleanup clears a ticket's own ticket-unqueued-* and ticket-refused-* troubles once the ticket stands at a terminal
